newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: Richina suggests why share price has risen.
newsitem.headline: Richina suggests why share price has risen.

text.p: Richina Pacific said on Tuesday it was not aware of any information which, if generally available to the public, might explain the recent variation in it share price.
Richina shares have risen 23 cents in just over a month, peaking at NZ$0.68 cents on Tuesday before closing at $0.64, up 19 cents from $0.45 on December 12.
However, in response to an enquiry from the New Zealand Stock Exchange, Richina gave the following possible reasons for the rise in its share price:

* "There have been a number of changes in the company over the past 18 months, as advised to the market. We believe there has been an increased understanding and changed market perception of the nature and direction of the company.

* Over the holiday season we were aware that national newspapers carried items that certain brokers had indicated that Richina Pacific shares were a share to invest in and further recent comments that the market was re-rating the shares as an entertainment stock, rather than a "construction stock".
* Our General Manager of Construction, Peter Deane, has been quoted in recent national press as indicating that he believes that the outlook for construction activities is positive.

* Our General Manager of Richina Underwater World, TJ O'Boyle, has also been quoted in response to enquires to the effect that Richina Underwater World has signed a memorandum of agreement to investigate the possibility of undertaking a further aquarium investment in Manila.
No commitments, other than to investigate a site and feasibility have been made and no contract has been signed.
Announcements will be made as appropriate when there is any contractual commitment. As reported, any building of the project is unlikely to commence before the last quarter of 1998.
* Our Underwater World Project in Beijing is proceeding according to plans and generally within budget with the scheduled opening in the third quarter of this year still anticipated.
We can only surmise that some investors may have made an assumption as to share value based on the actual completion and successful operation of the Beijing Aquarium.
* There has been speculation on the status of Midland-On-The Park project in Wellington and the construction/sale/leasing of an office tower.

While negotiations continue on all aspects of this project it remains a development project being undertaken in the normal course of our business and as material contractual matters likely to effect the share price are established we will advise the market.
No sale has been completed. We do not believe any of the matters noted above either individually of collectively account for the increase queried.

No matters are about to be announced save that we have entered into a conditional contract agreement to realise our investment in our parking operation subject to satisfaction of conditions. An announcement will be made immediately this happens."
